R7BG-bear-backcountry-0001.name: 1.1 km NE of Hay River
R7BG-bear-backcountry-0001.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).
R7BG-bear-backcountry-0001.parkWhat: pull off on an unnamed gravel road

evidence.t: Burn from 2023 (fire G90628), right here: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
SW facing slope, 10 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Unnamed wetland 90 m SW: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from Kahntah, about 48 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 58.47318, -120.324, pull off on an unnamed gravel road. Map links below.
Walk: 5.6 km W, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 31 m, about 115 min at 3 km/h.
Camp: flat ground 100 m N of the spot at 416 m (58.47288, -120.42001). Water: unnamed wetland 180 m S (estimate).

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Aug, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 7-56, Region 7B. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
